# Translink Express appoints four senior leaders after 32% growth

Translink Express Logistics has made four senior leadership appointments and announced plans to transform its Narborough headquarters into a major indoor palletised freight sortation centre.

 R By Ryan Fowler Publisher 

 1st September 2026 3 min read 

Translink Express Logistics has appointed four senior leaders as the Leicestershire logistics firm prepares for further growth ahead of its 40th anniversary.

The business has promoted Lee Barrett to head of traffic, Dan Green to the newly created role of head of project management and Shanice Walsh to head of operations.

Ryan Wallis has also joined the company as head of warehousing.

The appointments follow growth of almost 32% over the past 2 years, driven by new customer wins and existing customers increasing their use of Translink Express Logistics services.

The new management team will take on greater responsibility for the day-to-day running of the business, allowing the directors to focus more heavily on long-term strategy.

# Our Growth Board has a new member 👋 · 2026-07-29T00:00:00+00:00

Our Growth Board has a new member 👋

We're pleased to welcome Neil Midgley FCILT as our Director of Operations.

Neil brings 37 years of logistics, supply chain and manufacturing experience to the business, having held senior operational roles across third-party logistics, retail distribution, manufacturing and international freight.

His career includes leadership positions at GXO, Wincanton and Associated British Foods, where he oversaw everything from automated warehousing and large-scale transport operations to shared-user distribution networks and international logistics.

Alongside his operational experience, Neil holds a BSc (Hons) in Logistics and International Trade, is a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Logistics & Transport, and brings a wealth of industry expertise that will help shape the next phase of fulfilmentcrowd's growth.

As we continue to expand our global network and invest in our operations, Neil's experience will play an important role in delivering even greater value for our customers.

Welcome to the crowd, Neil! 🙌

fulfilmentcrowd appoints Neil Midgley as director of operations

By Dan Clough

Editor

14 Aug 2026

# fulfilmentcrowd appoints Neil Midgley as director of operations

By Dan Clough

14 Aug 2026

A new director of operations has been appointed at the Chorley based global tech-first fulfilment provider fulfilmentcrowd.

Neil Midgley, who spent 14 years at GXO (formally Wincanton), will lead core operational functions spanning network partners, sales, onboarding, and account management, ensuring alignment and efficiency as the business expands globally. 

The appointment comes as fulfilmentcrowd continues its growth plan following investment from Palatine Private Equity in May 2025.

Managing director Paul Taylor said: "Neil is already making a positive impact on how we operate, and we are looking forward to him playing an important role in delivering even greater value for our customers as we continue to grow.” 

Neil brings 37 years of logistics experience to fulfilmentcrowd, having previously managed large manufacturing fleets, as well as UK and European warehousing and transport operations. He also graduated in 2012 with a BSc honours degree in logistics and international trade.

# Key executive appointments for digital freight operator Ofload

Staff Writer August 7, 2026, 9:11 am August 7, 2026

An Ofload truck rolls out. Image: Ofload

Two new faces will be seen around the executive team table at Australian digital freight company Ofload this month with key commercial and operations appointments announced this week.

Karishma Bhatt will take the role of VP of Commercial and Rebecca Smith will become VP of Ops Enablement & Transformation.

Bhatt brings over a decade of logistics experience from roles at efm Logistics, FedEx, and CouriersPlease, and will oversee commercial strategy, new business, pricing, and shipper relationships.

Smith comes to Ofload after time at Woolworths Group where she led large-scale digital supply chain transformation. She will lead network reliability, service performance, and operational transformation at Ofload.

Ofload was launched in 2019 and has raised more than $100 million in funding and grown to more than 150 employees in that time.
